summary: A recursive function calls itself on a smaller input until it reaches a base case it can answer directly. Use it when a problem breaks into a smaller copy of itself.
notes: Every recursive function needs a base case, like if (n <= 1) return 1;, that makes no further call.
n / 10 gives a decimal in JavaScript, so Math.floor(n / 10) is needed to drop the last digit.
depth(-1) counts down past 0 and never reaches n === 0, so Node throws RangeError.
pitfall: Writing sumOfDigits(n / 10) without Math.floor keeps the decimal part, so sumOfDigits(2026) returns 10.885999999999992 instead of 10, with no error to warn you.
contrast: Python stops at about 1000 calls with RecursionError. Node's limit depends on the stack size, like Java, and running out gives RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded.
